output.name: Telvar
output.myth: When Aun cut the string and the sky drifted off over the water, the boats out on the Upper Sea lost their way in the dark, and the men on the rocks could see nothing but black. So Ennu, who sews the cloth for every kite, made one that carries a small oil lamp up the line on still nights. Hesk winds it slow, one turn for every hand's breadth, so it will not snatch. Tavo came down the cliff one night and tore at the cloth, laughing, and the lamp swung wild, but the cord held. Its light fell on the water, and the boats coming in from the Leeward dark saw the harbour and turned. Nethe the Drying Shag, to the west, who will not go in until the sun has dried her, went in by this light that night, and was not sorry. Sil saw it too from her drowned place, and was glad, though she did not say so. Mend your kites before the weather comes, child. A lamp on a string is the nearest thing to flying back that anyone has managed.
output.finding: From the Widow's Split-Tail in the north, go about one fist (10°) south to find the steady oil-lamp light, with the Drying Shag a little over half a hand-span to its west.
